structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Nebius can aggregate scarce AI infrastructure, but depends on upstream GPUs, power and datacenter delivery.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Long-duration demand supports downside resilience while concentrated buildout creates schedule and utilization sensitivity.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Customers can shift among hyperscalers, specialist GPU clouds or owned infrastructure if relative economics change.

discovery-weak-signals.name: contracted AI infrastructure demand
discovery-weak-signals.basis: large long-duration hyperscaler commitments materially improve forward demand visibility

discovery-weak-signals.name: contractedDemand
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Nebius disclosed a five-year Meta agreement for $12B of dedicated capacity plus up to $15B of additional available compute capacity, with delivery beginning in early 2027.

discovery-weak-signals.name: financingCapacity
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Nebius closed approximately $4.3375B of convertible senior notes in March 2026 for data-center buildout, AI-cloud investment, footprint expansion and key components including GPUs.

discovery-weak-signals.name: revenueScaleAcceleration
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Nebius's SEC-furnished Q2 2026 shareholder materials report Q2 group revenue of approximately $582M, up 454% year over year, and more than $2.3B of positive operating cash flow in the quarter.

discovery-weak-signals.name: contractEconomicsSignal
discovery-weak-signals.basis: The SEC-furnished shareholder letter states four Q2 deals averaged more than $1B each, Q2 deal ACV per MW exceeded $20M versus a stated 2026 base of $12M, and estimated payback for new Q2 deals was 1 year 10 months based on forecast costs and contracted future capacity.

discovery-weak-signals.name: supplyChainResilience
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Nebius disclosed a long-term Bloom Energy partnership using behind-the-meter fuel cells to reduce dependence on new transmission build, with 328 MW planned for operation in 2026 at the first U.S. deployment.

discovery-weak-signals.name: enterpriseDemandAndSovereignAI
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Nebius and Palantir announced on 2026-09-08 that Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner, with planned integration of Nebius compute and inference endpoints inside Palantir's enterprise perimeter for eligible commercial customers.

adversarial-red-team.name: financingRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: Contract-backed secured debt funds growth while increasing fixed claims on project cash flows.

adversarial-red-team.name: concentrationRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: Very large hyperscaler commitments can make customer-specific delivery and renewal outcomes material.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidenceInflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: Contract value should not be treated as equivalent to revenue, margin or free cash flow.

expectations-execution.name: capital execution
expectations-execution.basis: asset-backed financing tied to contracted cash flows reduces equity-only funding dependence for a deployment

expectations-execution.name: capitalExecution
expectations-execution.basis: Nebius disclosed a $775M senior secured facility backed by deployed GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows; together with customer cash flows it states the facility covers more than 100% of capex for the underlying deployment.

expectations-execution.name: contractedCapacityExecution
expectations-execution.basis: In the July 17 financing announcement Nebius said it had delivered the latest planned Microsoft capacity tranche and remained on track for remaining contracted tranches.

expectations-execution.name: operatingExecution
expectations-execution.basis: SEC-furnished Q2 2026 materials report Nebius AI cloud adjusted EBITDA margin of 50% and approximately $8B cash at quarter end, alongside the reported revenue acceleration.

expectations-execution.name: capacityExecution
expectations-execution.basis: The Q2 shareholder materials raised year-end 2026 contracted-power guidance to 5 GW and described capacity coming online through 2027.

expectations-execution.name: financingCapacity
expectations-execution.basis: Nebius subsequently closed $5.75B aggregate principal of new convertible senior notes on August 24, 2026, materially expanding financing capacity while also increasing future repayment and potential dilution exposure.

expectations-execution.name: capacityExecution
expectations-execution.basis: The Bloom agreement supplies a concrete power-delivery mechanism and a stated 328 MW 2026 operating target, improving source-addressed visibility into how Nebius intends to convert contracted AI demand into energized capacity; completion remains unverified.

expectations-execution.name: commercialDistributionExecution
expectations-execution.basis: The Palantir relationship provides a new enterprise distribution/integration path and explicit preferred-partner status, but the source describes future integration and does not prove production deployment or monetization.

sources.origin: Nebius Newsroom
facts: Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner.
Following integration, Palantir plans to bring Nebius compute and inference endpoints inside its enterprise perimeter for eligible customers.

sources.origin: Nebius Newsroom
facts: Nebius entered a senior secured debt facility of approximately $775 million.
The facility matures October 31, 2030 and is priced at SOFR plus 2.50%.
It is backed by deployed GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows from an investment-grade customer.
Nebius states the facility plus customer cash flows covers more than 100% of capex required for the underlying GPU deployment.

sources.origin: Nebius Newsroom / Palantir and Nebius partnership announcement
facts: Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner.
Following integration, Nebius compute and inference endpoints are intended to be available inside the Palantir enterprise perimeter for eligible customers.
The companies said they will work to bring new AI capacity online faster.

sources.origin: Nebius Newsroom / Meta AI infrastructure agreement
facts: Five-year agreement provides $12 billion of dedicated capacity to Meta across multiple locations starting early 2027.

Meta also committed to purchase additional available compute capacity across certain upcoming Nebius clusters up to $15 billion over five years, with Nebius intending first to sell that capacity to third parties.

sources.origin: U.S. SEC EDGAR / Nebius Group Form 6-K Exhibit 99.1
facts: Nebius closed $5.75 billion aggregate original principal amount of convertible senior notes: $3.45 billion of 0.50% notes due 2030 and $2.30 billion of 4.50% notes due 2034.

Nebius stated that net proceeds are intended to finance business growth including data-center construction/build-out, full-stack AI-cloud development, footprint expansion and procurement of key components including GPUs.
Nebius separately exchanged $400 million principal of 2029 notes and $400 million principal of 2031 notes for approximately 15.8 million Class A ordinary shares.

sources.origin: Nebius newsroom / joint Nebius-Bloom Energy announcement
facts: Nebius and Bloom Energy announced a long-term partnership to deploy Bloom fuel-cell systems for Nebius AI infrastructure.
The companies stated that 328 MW of installed capacity was planned to be operational in 2026.
The systems are designed to provide behind-the-meter electricity and reduce dependence on new transmission build, supporting faster time-to-power.

sources.origin: U.S. SEC EDGAR / Nebius Group N.V. Form 6-K Exhibit 99.1
facts: The AGM had 238,402,543 eligible Class A shares with one vote each and 33,455,053 eligible Class B shares with ten votes each; the classes voted together on all matters.
Arkady Volozh was re-appointed as an executive director with 377,275,928 votes for, 21,732,302 against and 4,071,963 abstained.
Shareholders approved designating the board for five years to issue Class A shares up to an additional 20% of issued share capital (excluding Class C shares).
Shareholders approved designating the board for five years to exclude existing-shareholder pre-emption rights for Class A share issuance.

sources.origin: Nebius Group N.V. newsroom / financing closing announcement
facts: Nebius announced the closing of two convertible senior note series with total aggregate original principal of $5.75 billion.
The 2030 notes have aggregate original principal of $3.45 billion and a 0.50% coupon.
The 2034 notes have aggregate original principal of $2.30 billion and a 4.50% coupon.
The initial purchasers exercised their additional-purchase options in full.

sources.origin: Nebius Group N.V. newsroom / Bloom Energy power partnership announcement
facts: Nebius and Bloom Energy announced an agreement to deploy Bloom fuel-cell technology for Nebius AI infrastructure.
The announcement states 328 MW of installed capacity was planned to be operational in 2026.
Nebius described the behind-the-meter system as reducing dependence on new transmission build and shortening time-to-power.

sources.origin: Nebius Group N.V. newsroom / Independence Missouri AI-factory approval announcement
facts: Independence City Council approved the Chapter 100 industrial-development incentive plan for Nebius's planned AI-factory campus.
Nebius said the approval enables it to proceed with construction.
The planned campus has potential capacity of up to 1.2 GW.

sources.origin: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Nebius Group N.V.
observedFacts: Q2 2026 group revenue approximately $582M, up 454% year over year.
Approximately $2.3B positive operating cash flow and approximately $8B cash ending Q2.
Nebius AI cloud adjusted EBITDA margin reported at 50%.
Four Q2 deals averaged more than $1B each; Q2 deal ACV per MW reported above $20M versus a $12M 2026 base.
Estimated payback for new Q2 deals stated as 1 year 10 months using forecast costs and contracted future capacity.
Year-end 2026 contracted-power guidance shown at 5 GW.

sources.origin: Nebius Group N.V.
observedFacts: Closed $3.45B principal of 0.50% convertible notes due 2030 and $2.3B principal of 4.50% convertible notes due 2034, totaling $5.75B aggregate principal.

sources.origin: Nebius Group N.V. / Bloom Energy
observedFacts: Nebius and Bloom Energy announced an agreement to deploy Bloom fuel-cell systems for Nebius AI infrastructure.
The systems are intended to provide behind-the-meter electricity and reduce dependence on new transmission build.
The companies stated that 328 MW of installed capacity was planned to be operational in 2026 at the first U.S. deployment.

sources.origin: Nebius Group N.V. / Palantir Technologies Inc.
observedFacts: Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner.
Following an integration period, Palantir plans to bring Nebius compute and inference endpoints inside the Palantir enterprise perimeter for eligible customers.
The companies stated they will work together to bring new AI capacity online faster.
